about: Tekken-style systems added to Street Fighter 6, offline only. One row per system. 'n/a' means the column does not apply to that row. Every cell must be filled. Heat follows Tekken 8: once per round, a 10 second timer that stops while the opponent is hit, no general damage bonus, and chip damage on block that cannot KO and that you win back by landing attacks. chip_pct_of_max and recover_pct_of_max_per_landed_attack are my estimates: Tekken's chip is 20% of the blocked attack's damage, which SF6 does not give us on a block yet. Rage follows Tekken 8 (season 3): active at 45 of 180 health (25%), +10% damage rounded down, and 70% less chip damage taken. A hit on a fighter who is not in Heat removes 30% of its damage from their recoverable health (from the Wavu wiki summary; whether the victim must be standing is not checked here). Heat Smash and Rage Art are stand-ins: they are damage bonuses on your next landed hit, armed with a key, not real moves. bonus_pct_of_max, armed_ticks and heat_start_heals_pct_of_pool are my estimates for fun, not Tekken's numbers. slowmo_fx slows the whole game for fx_frames screen frames at fx_speed_scale (1.0 = normal) when a Heat Smash or Rage Art lands. It is an experiment: it is off until the user tests it, and it turns itself off if the game refuses it. fx_method names which hook slows the game: global_speed, scene_time_scale or max_fps. hitstop_boost adds boost_frames to the hit freeze counter when a hit lands (big_boost_frames for a Heat Smash or Rage Art). heat_gauge draws a Tekken 8 style Heat gauge for each fighter: gauge_y_pct is its height on screen as a percent of screen height, gauge_w_pct its width as a percent of screen width, gauge_h_px its thickness in pixels and gauge_edge_pct its distance from the screen edge as a percent of screen width. The defaults are guesses to be tuned by eye in the panel.

rows.note: Tekken 8 Rage: at or under 25% health (45 of 180), every hit deals 10% more damage (rounded down) and chip damage taken is cut by 70%. Not possible here: Rage Art. The earlier numbers (20%, +15%) were verified working in game; these new numbers are untested. User played the Tekken 8 version offline and reported 'it feels good now' (2026-10-07). That is a general confirmation: the individual readouts were not reviewed one by one.

Tekken 8 Heat: press the key (P1 F1 = 112, P2 F2 = 113) to start Heat. It can be used once per round and lasts 10 seconds of running time (600 match ticks, about 60 per second); the timer stops while the opponent is in hitstun. Heat gives no damage bonus. A blocked hit costs the blocker chip damage that cannot KO; it is recoverable and is won back when the chipped fighter lands attacks. Not possible here: Heat Smash, Heat Dash, Heat Burst (2+3) input and Engager moves. Earlier version (+15% damage, 20 second cooldown, permanent chip) was verified in game; this version is a redesign and is untested. User played the Tekken 8 version offline and reported 'it feels good now' (2026-10-07). That is a general confirmation: the individual readouts were not reviewed one by one.
Tekken-style longer juggles by easing SF6's combo damage scaling. Not built: first find out what the probe says about combo_dm_air, and which data controls scaling.

Heat Smash stand-in: press the Heat key again while Heat is running to arm it for 2 seconds. The next hit that lands deals extra damage (15% of max health) and uses up your remaining Heat. If it does not land in time, the Heat is spent anyway. A blocked attack does not use it up. Not the real move: no animation, no armor. User played the Tekken 8 version offline and reported 'it feels good now' (2026-10-07). That is a general confirmation: the individual readouts were not reviewed one by one.

Rage Art stand-in: while in Rage, press the key (P1 F3 = 114, P2 F4 = 115) to arm it for 2 seconds, once per round. The next hit that lands deals extra damage (18% of max health), removes the opponent's recoverable health, wins back some of yours, and ends your Rage. If it does not land in time, Rage still ends. Not the real move: no animation or cinematic. User played the Tekken 8 version offline and reported 'it feels good now' (2026-10-07). That is a general confirmation: the individual readouts were not reviewed one by one.

Experimental impact slow-motion: when a Heat Smash or Rage Art lands, slow the game to 50% for about half a second by lowering the frame cap (so it looks choppy). Off by default. Test 2026-10-07: global speed and scene time scale did not visibly slow SF6; the frame cap method did. Speed and length can be changed live in the panel.
Weightier hits: first find out which field is the game's hit freeze and whether it can be written. The panel shows the live values of all three candidates.

Weightier hits: when a hit lands, add 3 frames to the game's hit freeze counter on both fighters (10 frames when a Heat Smash or Rage Art lands). On by default: the user tried it offline and said it feels good (2026-10-07). Sizes can be changed live in the panel and are saved.

Tekken 8 style Heat gauge, one per fighter, drawn on the game screen: P1 on the left, P2 on the right. While Heat runs it is an orange bar that drains over 10 seconds with the seconds left shown; it turns pale blue while the timer is paused (the opponent is being hit) and flashes red under 25%. When Heat is available it is a thin outline labelled HEAT. A thin bar under it shows recoverable health, and labels show RAGE, HEAT SMASH ARMED and RAGE ART ARMED. Position and size are adjustable in the panel and saved. Untested in game: the default position is a guess.
